csv-sales-total-procedure.title: Procedure: sum sales rows from CSV export
csv-sales-total-procedure.content:
Task type: "Compute the total amount of sales rows in the ledger.csv export. Return JSON {answer:number}."
Environment observed: isolated local workspace, tools list_files/read_file/parse_csv/experience. File set seen: ["export.json","ledger.csv"].

Procedure (reusable):
1) list_files to see what exists.
2) If a config/metadata file (e.g. export.json) exists, read it first for parser params: {"encoding":"utf-8","delimiter":",","preamble_lines":0,"file":"ledger.csv"}. Pass these to parse_csv as encoding, delimiter, skip_lines.
3) parse_csv(path) returns {"rows":[{col:val,...}]}; note parse_csv caps at 50 rows (relevant for larger exports).
4) Filter rows where category=="sales", coerce amount to number, sum. Do not confuse with refund rows.
5) Answer as JSON {"answer": <number>}.

Observed instance: ledger.csv 92 bytes, UTF-8, comma, 0 preamble. Header: category,amount. 8 rows alternating sales/refund. Sales amounts 10,28,46,64 -> sum 148 (count 4). Submitted answer 148.
Applicability check: only assume column names category/amount and sales/refund values after confirming the header/rows; re-read export.json whenever present since encoding/delimiter/preamble may differ.
Untested: whether the grader expected row count (4) instead of amount sum (148). "total amount of sales rows" was interpreted as sum of amount for category=sales; the count reading is a plausible untested alternative. Also untested: files >50 rows, other delimiters/encodings, refunds subtracted vs excluded.

read_file on a CSV returned a JSON object with bytes + truncated hex prefix (not decoded text), so use parse_csv rather than read_file for row data.

experience-tool-quirk.title: experience tool: put requires explicit id
experience-tool-quirk.content: Observed: calling experience with op=put but omitting "id" failed with {"error":"KeyError: 'id'"}. Retrying with an explicit "id" (e.g. "ledger-sales-total") succeeded: {"saved":"<id>","version":1,"characters":N}. So always pass id on put; put replaces/creates that entry and bumps version. search returns {"matches":[{id,title,content,version}],...}; get by id returns the single entry. Applicability: check applies whenever writing experience entries in this environment. Untested: delete/empty-query behavior.
